records.c: Install the main IRQ, initialise sound, set five load-specific pointers and initialise sprite and video state. Start with the local section index and map stride flag clear.
Call the section's timer and origin setup, refresh the HUD and clear the completion and scroll fields before redrawing the view.
Update the lives display and request a tune from the four-entry table at $295F when the selected tune has changed.
Read the joystick from CIA1 port A, wait for the raster tick and run the shared player update. Inspect stage collision flags and the player position before the shared action dispatch.
Clear the temporary refresh flag, patch the map window and refresh sprite coordinates and order before returning to the input poll.
Run the stage placement scanner, shared object pass, weapon selection, pause poll and timer. Update display and check the section completion or player death state.
Trigger an effect and wait, then increase the section counter. After four sections, branch to the level-cleared banner and load C.
Align the start column to a 64-column boundary, clear transient state and spend a life. The last local section restarts from its section setup.
Show game over, handle high scores and poll for a continuation. A continuation resets the score and lives; a rejected continuation returns to load A.
Display the level-cleared banner for round 4 and jump to the loader entry for file C.
Four tune IDs used by the section counter in load B.
Use the section number to fetch a pointer from $2975 and jump to the appropriate timer and scroll setup routine.
Four little-endian pointers for the load B section entry routines.
High byte of the first section setup handler.
Zero the origin and timer divider and set the first load B section's timer glyph and minute field.
Show the round-3-cleared banner and reset the timer and origin fields for the next section.
Set the map high column to one and initialise the next section's local scroll row and timer fields.
Clear the camera origin and timer fields before setting the final local section's timer glyph.
Read the current section's pointer from $2A15 and dispatch through $14.
Four little-endian pointers for initialising section-specific colours.
High byte of the first section palette handler.
Set the background registers and direct the row colour copier to $3F73.
Select the second section’s colours and its row table at $3F86.
Select the third section’s colours and its row table at $3F99.
Copy two sets of map rows into later stage positions before setting the final section’s colour values and row table.
Draw the score panel and add the 34-glyph message at $FA33.
The 34 glyphs of REWIND TAPE TO 0000 THEN PRESS PLAY, displayed in the restart prompt.
Copy columns 1 through $BD across ten map rows, advancing the two high pointer bytes by two for each row.
Clear the four weapon upgrade flags, restore the HUD icon pointers and clear the shadow count.
Recognise a new Space press, clear projectile activity and add two to the even weapon index with wrap at eight. Refresh the view and install the new weapon callbacks.
Choose the placement interval from the section index. Test low and high column and row bounds, dispatch visible placements and clear the work flags for placements outside the window.
Starting placement index for each of this load’s 4 sections. The scanner walks backward.
The scanner stops once its decremented placement index equals this section’s stop value.
Low bytes of the map columns compared with the current viewport column.
High bytes of those columns, compared with the active map page before checking X and Y.
Map row for each placement. The scanner tests it against the current row and its lower margin.
Work flags for each placement. The scanner clears the corresponding byte when its placement leaves the active viewport.
Map placement callbacks for this load. The scanner at $2B4B selects one of 35 pointers and jumps to it via $14.
High bytes of the interleaved placement callbacks, indexed by twice the placement record.
Update the stage special-map state, count 35 ticks and then preview a column-dependent map animation starting from the pointer in $14.
At the selected tick, allocate a type-$1B actor and initialise its fixed start coordinates and shape.
Begin with the placement’s stage helpers, then require an inactive flag and the 128-tick phase. Initialise a free sprite at the placement X and screen Y=$AF.
On the 64-tick phase, use an empty slot and initialise the actor at the placement’s screen coordinate with shape $67.
Start the same shape at an inactive placement on the 64-tick phase, clearing the per-slot counter in addition to hit and animation state.
Offset the spawn tick by $3F within a 128-tick period, allocate a slot at the placement’s row and initialise type $10.
Four starting screen X positions for the type-$14 spawn.
Four initial horizontal velocities.
Four initial vertical velocities.
Shapes paired with the four start positions.
On stage tick $C8 and while $277C is clear, allocate a free type-$0C slot and set its X to $A0.
Run the stage map helper before the four-slot placement path at $2E52.
Require an inactive encounter and the right stage phase, then allocate four slots together. Set the encounter-active flag and initialise the components.
Type bytes installed into the slots reserved by $2E52.
Hold the map origin, start a tune fade and count placement ticks. At 80, try to reserve eight slots for the set-piece actor.
X positions for each component of the eight-slot encounter.
Y positions paired with the encounter’s X positions.
Initial sprite pointers for the eight components.
Object types assigned to the eight slots.
Initial per-slot link or phase value stored in $9D,Y by encounter setup.
Run the placement precondition and lock the camera. Count until $7F before reserving five component slots.
Five object types set by the staged encounter at $2F51.
First sprite pointers for the corresponding five components.
Horizontal offsets from the five-part encounter origin.
Vertical offsets from that encounter origin.
Try the shared allocator on the 64-tick phase offset by $50, then change the new slot to type $0E.
Gate the shared allocator to stage ticks divisible by 128.
Place a new type-5 actor at the placement row and select a side and horizontal velocity with the random generator. The running spawn count changes its colour every eighth allocation.
Translate the current placement column into a sprite X coordinate relative to the camera and add the fine scroll contribution.
Convert the map row of the placement to sprite pixels relative to the camera.
The attribute byte returned by the shared map query at $127B for the tile read from the stage map.
Scan active logical slots and select each slot’s type handler. Subtract the camera movement from object coordinates and check the new position against the viewport limits before dispatch.
Jump through the pointer in $14 for the type or placement selected by the caller.
31 little-endian pointer entries indexed by twice the active slot type at $8E,X. The update pass at $316D skips a zero type before fetching its pointer.
High byte of the first object callback. Indexed by twice the active object type.
Left-side extent used by the collision rectangle code at $1740.
Per-type flag gating the collision callback in the shared pass at $1586.
Top-side extent read by $1740 when constructing an object’s tile rectangle.
Bottom-side extent read by $1740 to bound the vertical overlap test.
Inspect the local state at $3FE6. On state 2 select pointer 3, queue effect 1 and enter the shared encounter effects path.
Start with the ordinary slot colour, run the hit cooldown and switch to the hit colour when the pending hit flag is set.
Take the linked slot index from $9D,X, clear its activity flag and set its Y coordinate to $FA.
Compare the player against the component’s rectangular bounds and check for a free effect slot on contact.
Test the slot’s pending hit after checking its cooldown. Flash the sprite, clear the hit and advance the per-slot hit tally.
Mark the encounter active and select its hit or movement path from the slot’s cooldown and hit state.
Four initial pointers for the encounter, also used by its left movement phase.
Four pointers used in its alternate left-walking phase.
Four resting pointers restored at $37D3.
Mark the encounter active. A slot state of $FF enters the defeat effect and timed sequence; other states enter the live handler.
Five pose pointers for the leading component of the type-$16 encounter.
Five shape pointers for the second component.
Horizontal offsets for the second component’s poses.
Vertical offsets for the second component’s poses.
Five frame pointers for the third component.
Horizontal offsets for the third component’s poses.
Vertical offsets for the third component’s poses.
Check player overlap, then transform a hit into type $0B with yellow colour and shape $AA before applying velocity.
Advance the timer, sample the map above the object and check contact when the tile and hit state permit.
Award a score unit for a pending hit and replace the object using the shared effect.
Test player contact, then award a score unit and set the effect type, shape, colour and sound when the actor has been hit.
Update the pickup’s shape and at one-in-four raster ticks try a free slot for a particle with random offsets.
Set its placement flag active and decrement the object’s Y position until it reaches $A8.
Mark the placement active and advance the sprite’s early frames once per eighth tick. Select the next path once the shape reaches $A0.
Check player overlap and check the parent slot for type $18. Reverse the child’s horizontal velocity on its mid-cycle tick.
Retain the placement’s active flag and increment the shape on every eighth countdown tick until its movement state.
Eight sprite pointers selected by the type-$09 animation phase.
Test player contact and handle a new hit, including colour change, cooldown and sound $0B.
Read the stage tile beneath the object and use separate motion and hit paths according to the tile and slot colour.
Increase the BCD score when the slot’s hit flag is set. The colour-7 actor takes a separate response from the ordinary shared effect.
Fill 40 cells per row in colour RAM. Read the colour from each of 19 palette entries through $14.
Palette for the first 19 stage rows of the first section.
Row colours selected by the second section’s setup.
Row colour values selected by the third section.
Row colour values for the final local section.
Sample the map $15 pixels above the player and test for tile attribute 3. Set downward movement if airborne or enter the death routine otherwise.
